script: NBA teams that added too much TALENT and got worse! One team once built a roster so stacked it looked like a video game. The Portland Trail Blazers already had Scottie Pippen and Rasheed Wallace along with veteran center Arvydas Sabonis. And that group pushed the Los Angeles Lakers to a Game Seven in the Western Conference Finals, where Portland led by fifteen points in the fourth quarter. But that fifteen-point lead is the reason this whole story exists. The Blazers collapsed and lost eighty-nine to eighty-four, then watched the Lakers go on to win the championship. So Portland's general manager Bob Whitsitt made a call. If his team couldn't get past Shaquille O'Neal, he would add more size to stop him. So he traded for All-Star big man Shawn Kemp by giving up Brian Grant, then shipped a young Jermaine O'Neal to Indiana to land another All-Star big man in Dale Davis. But the timing of these two trades is what turned them into a mistake. Portland was now two players deep at every single position, and on paper this was one of the deepest teams ever assembled. Kemp showed up out of shape though, and averaged just six points a game, so the crowded roster never clicked. Portland finished fifty and thirty-two, then drew the Lakers again in the playoffs, this time in the very first round. And the team that loaded up to finally beat Los Angeles got swept three games to nothing, doing worse than the year before they added two All-Stars.
